dedupe_keys.name: agriculture and livelihood flood impact assessment in myanmar after cyclone komen 2015

description: This case study is the joint assessment of how the floods and landslides that followed Cyclone Komen, which made landfall in Bangladesh on 30 July 2015, affected agriculture and rural livelihoods in Myanmar. National figures cited in it record 122 deaths, up to 1,624,000 people displaced and 525,330 hectares of farmland inundated. It was requested by Myanmar's Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation and Ministry of Livestock, Fisheries and Rural Development and co-led by FAO and WFP under the Food Security Sector with UN Women, World Vision, CESVI, CARE, JICA and LIFT. It covers the six most-affected regions and states: Ayeyarwady, Bago, Chin, Magway, Rakhine and Sagaing. The report is a free PDF. It found almost 400,000 hectares flooded in Ayeyarwady, Bago and Rakhine, monsoon paddy making up 89% of damaged crops with production losses of at least 30% expected, about 2,500 hectares destroyed by landslides in Chin, sediment on fields, lost seeds, fertiliser and tools, damaged irrigation, over 250,000 animals lost, and falling farm labour income, with women's wages already almost 20% below men's. Caveats: it is a rapid assessment with stated limitations, and no licence is given. For simulation it supplies observed flood impacts on rice, livestock and irrigation for calibrating agricultural exposure and recovery models. It is related to the FAO damage and loss methodology record in this catalogue.
